name: Done ADHD
one_liner: Online ADHD evaluation and medication management for adults by video, from a company whose founder was convicted over Adderall prescribing.
best_for: Adults who want a video ADHD evaluation and have checked Done's current status first
Adults already diagnosed with ADHD who want medication follow-ups by video
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People who want therapy or coaching for ADHD rather than medication
Anyone who wants a provider without a recent federal criminal case over stimulant prescribing
short_description: Done is a subscription telehealth service for adult ADHD diagnosis and medication management.
long_description: Done (Done Global, donefirst.com) is a subscription telehealth service for adults with ADHD: you complete an assessment, see a clinician by video and, if diagnosed, get ongoing medication management. In November 2025 a federal jury in San Francisco convicted founder and former CEO Ruthia He and former clinical president David Brody of illegally distributing Adderall over the internet and conspiring to commit health care fraud; in July 2026 He was sentenced to six years in prison and Brody to two years, each with a $1 million fine. Neither the court reports nor the press coverage say whether Done still treats patients, and its current price could not be verified. There are no published studies of Done's own service.

faqs.q: How does Done's ADHD evaluation work?
faqs.a: Done's evaluation includes completing questionnaires about your symptoms, history, and functioning, followed by a video appointment with a licensed clinician. If you meet criteria for ADHD, they can discuss treatment options including medication.

Done prescribes FDA-approved ADHD medications including stimulants when clinically appropriate. However, controlled substance prescribing through telehealth has faced regulatory changes since 2022. Availability and requirements vary by state. Verify current policies before enrolling.

Done offers subscription plans for ongoing care, typically $199-299/month. Some insurance plans may be accepted. Medication costs are separate. Self-pay options are available for those without coverage.

faqs.q: Is Done legitimate for ADHD treatment?
faqs.a: Done uses licensed clinicians for ADHD evaluation and treatment. However, like other ADHD telehealth platforms, it has faced scrutiny over prescribing practices. Do your research, understand the limitations, and ensure you're comfortable with the care model.

availability.note: Founder and former clinical president convicted in November 2025 and sentenced in July 2026 over Adderall distribution through the platform; whether Done still takes new patients is not confirmed.

patient_summary: You fill in an online assessment, then see a clinician by video who can diagnose ADHD and prescribe medication, with follow-ups on a monthly membership. The company's leaders were convicted in 2025 over Adderall distribution through the platform, so check whether it is taking patients and how it prescribes before you sign up. The current membership price could not be verified.
